newsitem.title: FRANCE: French trawlers to defy Guernsey fishing ban.
newsitem.headline: French trawlers to defy Guernsey fishing ban.

text.p: A French maritime surveillance boat will accompany French trawlers near the Channel island of Guernsey from Monday in a row with Britain over fishing rights, French diplomatic sources said on Sunday.

The sources said Guernsey authorities had gone back on a two-year-old arrangement which allowed French trawlers to operate in the island's waters in return for rights for Guernsey fishermen to fish in French waters.
They said French fishermen were determined to ignore warnings that they would be prosecuted if they kept fishing near Guernsey after December 1.
"French trawlers must not be excluded from this area and France will show its determination," a diplomat said.

The sources said French maritime authorities had decided to despatch the civilian surveillance boat Coriandre with the trawlers to monitor developments. The boat was not a navy ship and was unarmed, they said.
They said Foreign Minister Herve de Charette had written to his British counterpart on November 14 with proposals to solve the dispute, but had yet to receive a reply.
